title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
description: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing in Tonic Solfa to MENDELSSOHN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, all three verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley's Christmas hymn was published in 1739, beginning 'Hark, how all the welkin rings'; George Whitefield changed the opening to the words sung today. The tune comes from a cantata Felix Mendelssohn wrote in 1840 for a festival celebrating Gutenberg's printing press; William H. Cummings fitted it to these words in the 1850s.
underlay: Hark! the her-ald an-gels sing_ Glo-ry to the new-born King; Peace on earth, and mer-cy mild,_ God and sin-ners re-con-ciled! Joy-ful, all ye na-tions, rise,_ Join the tri-umph of the skies;_ With th’an-gel-ic host pro-claim, Christ is_ born in Beth-le-hem! Hark! the her-ald an-gels sing Glo-ry_ to the new-born King.

lines: Peace on earth, and mercy mild,
Join the triumph of the skies;
Late in time behold Him come,
Veiled in flesh the Godhead see;
Pleased as man with man to dwell,
Hail the heaven-born Prince of Peace!
Light and life to all He brings,
Risen with healing in His wings.
Mild He lays His glory by,
Born that man no more may die,
Born to raise the sons of earth,
Born to give them second birth.
